title: The Lost Crowns
snippet:
The Lost Crowns -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The Lost Crowns* is a trilogy of episodic DLCs for *Dark Souls II*, released for the PS3, Xbox 360, and PC. The episodes can be purchased separately for $9.99 each, or all three can be purchased through Steam, PSN, and Xbox Live for $24.99.

title: The Lost Crowns
snippet:
The Lost Crowns -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : There are no requirements to access the DLC, other than having access to the Primal Bonfire or location where the warp shrine is located. Each warp shrine leads to a cavernous room containing a locked door.

Players who own the DLC will receive a key item that will allow them to open the door. Players who don't own the DLC are still able to play through parts of the new content, but only as a summoned phantom.

title: The Lost Crowns
snippet:
The Lost Crowns -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - in_game_reward 
 in_game_reward : Upon obtaining all three DLC-related crowns and Vendrick's crown, a special ability is granted by speaking to Vendrick in the Undead Crypt: the ability prevents the player character from hollowing upon death if any of the crowns was worn, much like the Ring of Life Protection. However, any souls held will be lost.

In addition, crowns obtained in previous playthroughs do not count towards getting the reward. This means all the crowns must be obtained in a single playthrough for the ability to be granted. The ability does not carry over to the next playthrough.

title: Vendrick
snippet:
Vendrick -  Dark Souls II - boss - plot 
 plot : After an untold amount of time in confinement, the King of Drangleic remains a hollowed husk of his former self. The player may choose to spare the king, leaving him to wander eternally, or slay him and end his misery.

Using the Ashen Mist Heart, the Bearer of the Curse may also enter the Memory of the King, where they may interact with King Vendrick as he was before he went hollow. Bitter and grieving his failures, Vendrick tells the Bearer to seek the crowns of old kings of yore. Once they have brought him all the crowns, Vendrick will unlock their power, making the Bearer of the Curse immune to the hollowing effects of the curse. He advises the Bearer of the Curse to seek a third path beyond Light and Dark, echoing his brother.

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet:
Burnt Ivory King -  Dark Souls II - boss - fight_overview 
 fight_overview : The player will not immediately face the Ivory King after passing through the fog door and dropping into the Old Chaos. Instead, the player will face three waves of Charred Loyce Knights who will emerge from the three portals around the arena. The knights will be a random mix of halberd, sword, or pyromancy users. During the first wave, three Knights will spawn. After a short period of time, several more will spawn, then several more shortly thereafter.

Finding the three uncorrupted Knights from around Eleum Loyce will be an immense help in the fight. Throughout the entire battle, the Knights will periodically freeze the portals, preventing Charred Knights from spawning.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Finally, the Bearer of the Curse travels to Frozen Eleum Loyce, once ruled by the Ivory King. Built to contain the Old Chaos, the city was abandoned and froze over when its king vanished into the chaos. Guided by the last child of the Abyss, Alsanna, Silent Oracle, the Bearer of the Curse seeks out the remaining knights of Eleum Loyce to gain their help in braving the Old Chaos. Finding the Burnt Ivory King there, the Bearer of the Curse defeats him and claims his crown.

Once the Bearer of the Curse has found all three crowns of old, along with Vendrick's own crown, the fallen king will unleash the hidden power of the crowns, making the Bearer of the Curse immune to the hollowing effects of the curse. Bidding the Bearer to seek strength, and asking them whether allowing the flames to fade is truly their only choice, the king sends the Bearer of the Curse on their way.

 dark_souls_ii : Hollowing in *Dark Souls II* is similar to the previous game, with a few key differences:

#Being hollow does not prevent being invaded by NPCs and other players.
#Each death suffered will reduce the player's max HP in increments of 5%. This will continue until it caps at 50% of maximum HP, unless the player has a sin level of wretch, which will cap it at 5%. With the Ring of Binding equipped, the HP cap is halved.

title: Pontiff Knight
snippet: When Pontiff Sulyvahn plotted to control Irithyll, he corrupted their leaders thanks to the unquenchable Profaned Flame that he found in the ruins of the Profaned Capital. After turning the captains of the army of Irithyll into sorcerers in his service, Sulyvahn also influenced the knights they led, gifting them golden crowns as they helped him seize power. After he took power, the knights would serve as Sulyvahn's watchful eyes and punitive blades. When Aldrich and his Deacons attacked Irithyll, the Pontiff Knights were all slain, and now they are frigid spirits brought back to life by the Pontiff's necromancy. Their swords are now gnawed by the insects of the deep spawned by the Evangelists, and the knights continuously spit dark souls as their bodies were hit and filled by the sorceries of the deacons.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: He gathered an army of deacons, who cast off their red robes and crowns—symbolic of their clerical duties— for new dark-blue ones and swore fealty as Aldrich Faithful, their venerance of the Deep finally codified under Aldrich's banner. He then marched on Irithyll, home to the old gods of Anor Londo and the residence of Chief Deity Gwyndolin. Likely forcing his way through the city's magical barrier, he would confront the forces of Pontiff Sulyvahn, who had no intention of relinquishing his power and authority over the city. From the battle that ensued, Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and forcing him into capitulation. Seemingly, the two eventually struck a deal: the Pontiff would maintain some control over lower Irithyll; in exchange, Aldrich would be granted access to Gwyndolin, who was imprisoned by the Pontiff within the old Cathedral of Anor Londo.

The township has become filled with enemies (specifically Bloatheads, Bloathead Sorcerers, and a Chained Prisoner) as the Abyss spreads, and is seemingly deserted.

One of the Four Knights of Gwyn, Artorias the Abysswalker, arrived in Oolacile to rescue Dusk of Oolacile from Manus, Father of the Abyss, but fell victim to the Abyss. By the time the Chosen Undead found him, Artorias was hostile and engaged them in combat. After the Chosen Undead defeated the brave knight, they finish what Artorias had started, continuing through Oolacile Township and onward, eventually defeating Manus and rescuing Dusk.

title: Lost Sinner
snippet:
Lost Sinner -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : The Lost Sinner is a forgotten entity who imprisoned herself for unknown sins committed long ago. Donning the Penal Set, she lives in constant agony and shame. The true nature of her weapon is unknown, even to the Lost Sinner herself. Those who choose this sword will share the burden of the Lost Sinner's misdeeds.

Just like the other Old Ones, the Lost Sinner is possessed by one of the great lords of Lordran, specifically the Witch of Izalith, as suggested by the Chaos Bug from Lost Izalith in *Dark Souls* and the Old Witch Soul she drops in NG+ (which can also be traded for a Chaos Blade), as well as having Pyromancers assist her in battle. Additionally, equipping the Penal Handcuffs enhances pyromancies.

Gods Grave -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - environment 
 environment : While having no textures or objects, rudimentary level geometry contained in the map data for Dark Souls 3 resembles the Catacombs from Dark Souls 1 and/or the section of Lost Izalith containing the Bed of Chaos. Despite no assets pertaining to the area itself, references to the area are found in data strings within objects that were later used within the Ringed City: the gravestones located in the first section of the Ringed City that block arrows from the archers, and strange pots which have roots growing out of them.

This being said, it is known that the top half of the area was in a forest, for standard trees present in various areas of the final game are also present here.

What was in the bottom half of the area is still unknown.

title: Spear of the Church
snippet:
Spear of the Church -  Dark Souls III - boss - plot 
 plot : Peculiar in several ways, this boss fight is the penultimate mandatory battle in *The Ringed City DLC*, as well as within the whole game. As such it takes place within the church near the end of the titular city.

At first, the only enemy present is Judicator Argo, although his only goal is to summon three special enemies, which he will do regardless of the player's actions: a Spear of the Church and two Church Guardians, one for each phase of the boss fight. They are a support enemy unique to this battle, resembling Painting Guardians from *Dark Souls*, but using a regular player model instead of a unique character model.

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet:
Burnt Ivory King -  Dark Souls II - boss - attacks 
 attacks : **Sword Buff**: Periodically throughout the fight, the King will take a few seconds to buff his sword with magic. Unlike the Smelter Demon, he does not have enhanced defenses during this period, which offers the chance to attack him with impunity.

**Ice Explosion**: Only used when the King has buffed his sword. He will slam the point into the ground, emitting a series of highly-damaging ice spikes in a circle around himself. Easily avoided by moving back from the King when he turns his sword upside down.

**Impale**: Only used with the buffed sword. Similar to Sir Alonne's impale attack, the King will charge up for a moment before lunging at the player. If he connects, he will lift the player on his sword, draining a large amount of health, after which he'll throw the player away.

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet:
**Lunging Slash**: This attack will pass straight through shields when his sword is buffed, and is a danger because it will not knock the player down, opening the player up to his follow-up spin attack.

**Jumping Spin**: The King will jump into the air, spinning 360 degrees before slashing with his sword. He often uses this after his lunging slash.

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet:
At an unknown point, an ancient Chaos was discovered deep below the land. Legend holds that the Ivory King used his magnificent soul to build Eleum Loyce and contain the spread of Chaos. A grand cathedral was built in an attempt to appease the raging flame, but the Chaos would not be sated. As a precaution, various knights and golems were posted throughout the Garrison Ward to lead the advance on the swollen flame on his orders. Other knights were ordered to delve into the depths of Chaos to exterminate the terrible things that dwelt there, but not one of the knights returned.

Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce without a word, leaving everything to Alsanna. He traveled deep into the Chaos until he and his knights were corrupted by the flames. At some point after the King's departure, the ivory gates of the city were flung open, and the land grew cold and lifeless.

title: Dusk Crown Ring
snippet:
Removing the ring will not restore the lost health. This can be useful as a quick way to activate the Red Tearstone Ring.

The ring can be used to reduce fall damage. This is because fall damage is calculated by taking a percentage of the player's maximum HP. This means that the player takes only half of the usual fall damage with the ring equipped, and can use it with no consequences if their HP is less than 50%. Note that this does not allow you to fall longer distances.

title: Dusk Crown Ring
snippet:
Dusk Crown Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - general_information 
 general_information : The Dusk Crown Ring grants 50% more sorcery, miracle, and pyromancy castings (rounded down), but halves the user's maximum HP. Upon removing the ring, the number of castings will be scaled down to about 67% (rounded down). The underlying conversion seems to keep track of the number of casts with the ring equipped. Hence it is possible to equip the ring and have a 0 casting spell to be increased to 1 cast.

The reduction of HP is applied before HP boosting items. This results in having roughly 60% maximum HP with the Ring of Favor and Protection, 52.5% maximum HP with the Tiny Being's Ring and 55% with the Mask of the Mother, these items can also be stacked to further reduce the HP reduction.

Removing the ring will not restore the lost health. This can be useful as a quick way to activate the Red Tearstone Ring.

title: Dusk Crown Ring (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Dusk Crown Ring (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - ring - effect 
 effect : For the majority of spells, equipping this ring will reduce its FP consumption by a value between 20% and 25%, while reducing HP by 15%, rounded down. However, wearing this ring does not affect spells which constantly drain one's FP while held, such as Fire Surge and Divine Pillars of Light.

Generally speaking, the higher the base FP cost of a spell is, the greater the FP cost reduction that it receives is likely to be after equipping the ring. For example, the cost reduction of a spell with a low spell cost, such as Deep Soul, will probably be closer to 20% (or even below 20%, in some cases), while that of a spell with high FP consumption, such as Tears of Denial, will likely be closer to 25%.
